# `enabled` reference

<Warning>

This page documents a **draft** for a feature currently gated behind the
`enabled_meta_argument` experiment (not yet released in any stable version
of Terraform). Experiments are subject to change or removal without notice,
and this page should not be published until the feature stabilizes. Refer
to the [`terraform` block's `experiments` argument](/terraform/language/block/terraform#experiments)
and the [Terraform changelog](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for the current status.

</Warning>

By default, a [`resource` block](/terraform/language/block/resource) configures one real infrastructure object, and a [`module` block](/terraform/language/block/module) includes a child module's contents in the configuration exactly once.

Use the `enabled` meta-argument to turn that single instance on or off based on a condition, without changing how the resource or module is addressed. This differs from the common `count = <condition> ? 1 : 0` pattern, which works but makes the resource's address conditionally indexed (`aws_instance.example[0]` instead of `aws_instance.example`), forcing a `terraform state mv` any time the condition's truthiness changes historically, and requiring index-aware syntax such as `aws_instance.example[0].id` or `try(aws_instance.example[0].id, null)` everywhere the resource is referenced.

## Usage

The `enabled` meta-argument accepts a boolean value. When `true` (or omitted), the block behaves exactly as it would without `enabled` at all: one instance, addressed without an index. When `false`, Terraform creates zero instances, and the block's address becomes unavailable, exactly as if the block were commented out — but referencing it directly still evaluates to `null` rather than raising an error, so the existing `try()`/[`coalesce()`](/terraform/language/functions/coalesce) idiom used with `count` continues to work unchanged.

```hcl
variable "kms_master_key_id" {
  type    = string
  default = null
}

module "kms" {
  source  = "kn47ytv9mv/kms/aws"
  enabled = var.kms_master_key_id == null
}

locals {
  # Falls back to the key this module creates only when the caller
  # didn't supply their own. No indexing, no try()-around-an-index.
  kms_master_key_id = coalesce(var.kms_master_key_id, try(module.kms.arn, null))
}
```

You cannot use both `enabled` and `count`, or both `enabled` and `for_each`, in the same block. Use `enabled` when a block has exactly one meaningful instance that should conditionally exist; use [`count`](/terraform/language/meta-arguments/count) or [`for_each`](/terraform/language/meta-arguments/for_each) when it can have more than one.

### Referring to a disabled instance

Unlike `count = 0` (which makes the whole resource evaluate to an empty list, `[]`) or `for_each = {}` (an empty map, `{}`), a resource or module with `enabled = false` evaluates to `null`. This keeps its shape consistent with the `enabled = true` case — a single object — rather than switching between an object and a collection depending on the condition:

```hcl
output "key_arn" {
  # Works whether module.kms exists or not, and never needs an index:
  value = try(module.kms.arn, null)
}

output "key_arn_guarded" {
  # A ternary guarded on the same condition short-circuits cleanly too,
  # since the untaken branch's attribute access is never evaluated:
  value = var.kms_master_key_id == null ? module.kms.arn : null
}
```

### Expressions in `enabled`

The `enabled` meta-argument accepts boolean [expressions](/terraform/language/expressions). Like `count` and `for_each`, its value must be known before Terraform performs any remote resource operations — it cannot depend on an attribute that's only known after applying the configuration, such as an ID generated by a remote API.

You cannot use [sensitive values](/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data) in `enabled`, for the same reason you cannot use them in `for_each`: whether an instance exists at all is always visible in plan output, so a sensitive condition would necessarily leak.

## Supported constructs

You can use `enabled` in the following Terraform configuration blocks:

- [`resource` blocks](/terraform/language/block/resource)
- [`data` blocks](/terraform/language/block/data)
- [`ephemeral` blocks](/terraform/language/block/ephemeral)
- [`module` blocks](/terraform/language/block/module)

`enabled` is not currently supported in `action` blocks.
